summary: Built a backfill pipeline that imports historical Pi and Claude Code sessions into the gizmo journal for the gizmo workspace. Created a Claude Code adapter (translating tool_use/tool_result/thinking/text into the existing journal schema, with noise filtering for slash-command plumbing), a backfill module that walks both session stores and stamps provenance (`source: pi-archive | claude-code`) on each segment, and a CLI entry point. Fixed the Pi normalizer to use the canonical branch (not the full entry tree, which double-included retried prose) and to drop empty assistant turns. All 34 memory tests pass and the dry run imports 60 Pi + 4 Claude Code segments cleanly.
decisions: Scope: backfill only the gizmo workspace (59 Pi sessions + 4 Claude Code sessions), not other projects — chosen by the user to limit blast radius.

Both Pi and Claude Code sources are imported — Claude Code's ~5,900 entries are kept despite needing a new adapter because Pi's format is identical to gizmo's so Pi costs almost nothing, and the two schemas map cleanly onto the existing journal types.

Claude Code tool_result blocks must be split off from `user` messages into the `toolResult` role before normalization; otherwise ~1,921 tool payloads get journaled as user prose and poison the knowledge-layer signal.
Idempotency uses the source's stable per-entry id (Pi entry id, Claude `uuid`) via the existing `resumeAfter()` dedup, so backfill is safely re-runnable and cannot double-import.
Backfilled segments carry a `source:` provenance field in their frontmatter so downstream knowledge extraction can distinguish imported history from live sessions.
Pi imports use `SessionManager.getBranch()` rather than `getEntries()` so retried and abandoned branches don't double up in the journal.
`assistantSection` now returns `string | undefined` and the normalizer drops empty assistant turns instead of emitting bare `## assistant` headers.
errors: Initial dry run produced duplicated prose in Pi segments: cause was importing the full entry tree (including retried branches) instead of the canonical branch; fixed by switching backfill to `getBranch()`.

Initial dry run produced empty `## assistant` sections: cause was `assistantSection` always emitting a header even when the turn carried only a stop reason; fixed by making the section return `undefined` when empty and the normalizer skipping it.
